ROS in bone resorption and formation

The role of ROS in bone resorption and formation. Excessive ROS promotes bone resorption (A) and impairs bone formation (B) by modulating multiple osteogenic signaling pathways. In osteoclasts, ROS activate the RANKL–RANK signaling cascade, promoting differentiation and resorptive function, and induce autophagy to further enhance bone degradation. In osteoblasts, ROS causes mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis, sequesters β-catenin to suppress osteogenic differentiation, and upregulates RANKL while downregulating osteoprotegerin (OPG), indirectly augmenting osteoclastogenesis. In bone marrow stromal cells (BMSCs), ROS drive adipogenic commitment and trigger a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), thereby disrupting normal lineage differentiation and regenerative capacity. Collectively, ROS-induced dysregulation of the coupling between bone formation and resorption compromises the bone healing process. HSC, hematopoietic stem cell; RANKL, receptor activator of nuclear factor κB ligand; TRAF6, TNF receptor-associated factor 6; PI3K, phosphoinositol-3 kinase; MAPK, mitogen-activated protein kinase; IKK complex, IκB kinase complex; NF-κB, nuclear factor κB; IKK-β, IκB kinase β; c-Fos, cellular FBJ murine osteosarcoma viral oncogene homolog; c-Jun, cellular avian sarcoma virus 17 oncogene homolog; AKT, protein kinase B; ER, endoplasmic reticulum; LC3, microtubule-associated protein 1A/1B-light chain 3; TFEB, transcription factor EB; Beclin1, BCL2-interacting protein 1; M-CSF, macrophage colony-stimulating factor; BMAds, bone marrow adipocytes; IL-12, interleukin-12; TNFα, tumor necrosis factor α; PPARγ, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ; CEBPs, CCAAT/enhancer-binding proteins; AMPK, AMP-activated protein kinase; CBP/p300, CREB-binding protein/p300; FoxOs, forkhead box Os; TCF, T-cell factor; sRANKL, soluble RANKL; ALP, alkaline phosphatase
